linkedin_draft:
We have redesigned root.vc — for one week — as a Victorian natural history museum.

The conceit: every portfolio company has been accessioned as a specimen, complete with its Latin binomial, habitat, accession number, and field note. Esper is now Esper devicensis, sighted in enterprise device fleets. Wildtype Foods becomes Wildtypa salmonia, cultivated in bioreactors. Kayhana orbitalis lives in low earth orbit, where one would expect to find it. Sixty-three specimens in all. We accessioned the entire portfolio.

The team are the museum's curators. Avidan is Director and Founding Curator. Lee is the Curator of Devtools and Software Specimens. Chrissy is Keeper of Electrical Specimens. Kane handles the Mechanical Artifacts hall. Zodi is Associate Curator of Intelligence Studies, which feels right. Ben is the Registrar — which is also true in real life. Laelah runs the Conservation Studio.

The Founding Charter is the firm's actual thesis, printed between brass studs. Operating economics — fund size, check size, reserves ratio — sit in a small grid below it, the way a museum lists its operating hours. Inquiries go to the Registrar's Office at hello@root.vc, which routes to a real inbox. Vacancies in the Department lists our open Associate role.

We always carry an in-world doorway to past drops; this week it is the Archive Wing, accessible through the East Door, which preserves earlier exhibitions including the original CLI terminal (1st installed Feb 2021) and the GeoCities salon (Oct 2021).

root.vc is one engineering experiment that resets every Monday. This is the first proper drop of the new cycle. Come walk the galleries.

Seeding bold engineers — since 2015, and continuing.
